reuse.why: Reuses getWorstCaseAmount and the matcher's getApproxNumberThreshold, but adds a new getExpectedAmount beside the existing getScheduledAmount (which already does the null/number/range expected-amount dispatch) instead of extending it.

duplication.why: It removes five inline null/number/range ternaries, but getExpectedAmount re-implements the same dispatch that getScheduledAmount already contains, leaving two parallel expected-amount functions.

placement.why: The rule is placed in shared/schedules.ts next to the other amount helpers and server sites call it, which fits the layering.

scope.why: Only the amount rule and its call sites are touched.

maintainability.why: Server paths now share one definition, but the existing getScheduledAmount used by the API's expectedAmount and by the desktop-client balance/schedule views still lacks the approximate rule, so two functions answer the same question differently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts adds getExpectedAmount instead of changing getScheduledAmount, which api-models.ts toExternal and desktop-client SchedulesTable/Balance/MobileSchedulesPage/SchedulesListItem/useScheduleEdit keep using.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts getExpectedAmount is getScheduledAmount's null->0 / number / getWorstCaseAmount dispatch under a new name with an op parameter, rather than one function.

one_place.where: The approximate rule lives in getExpectedAmount (used by schedules/app.ts, forecast-schedules.ts, schedule-template.ts, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions) but not in getScheduledAmount, used by api-models.ts expectedAmount and the desktop-client schedule/balance views.
